To the Esteemed: Lords Commissioned Directors at the Assembly of Seventeen from the Respective Chambers Representing the General Chartered Dutch East India Company at Amsterdam, Ruling Lords and Commanding Gentlemen. Since our letter over Persia of the 1st of January of this year from Ammerongen, eighteen days thereafter (God be praised) here over Malacca from Batavia and Japan came to arrive, the ships Rammekens, Vlaerdinge, Loosdijnen, Gulde Leeuw, and the Hooker De Pimpelmees, from both places having also brought, 28,961 pieces of gold cobangs [Indian currency], 62,500 pounds of staff copper, 200,293 pounds of pepper, 10,000 pounds of clove nails, some porcelains, lacquerware, and provisions, to the value of 646,461 guilders [modern equivalent: Dutch currency], 13 shillings, 12 pence. And for the year 1671, for the Japanese Trade from here has been petitioned 1,200 bales of silk, 80 thereof of floret yarn, 2,400 pieces of striped and plain giegans [type of fabric], 2,000 pieces of addathaijs [type of fabric], 1,200 pieces of coarse allegias [type of fabric], 7,500 pounds of catechu, though that in Pattana costs 1 1/16 and in Surat 3/6 stuivers [modern equivalent: Dutch currency] per pound, therefore up to 37,500 pounds (being the whole Japanese request enlarged), 1,000 pounds of borax and 362,500 pounds of sugar, all of which in equal measure we shall be able to fulfill, just as also the request from there of the previous year, and still 165 bales of silk more have been fulfilled, though the latter somewhat dearer than those of years before in the time that could be gathered here for that trade, arising from such contingencies of the times as with our aforementioned letter your Excellency's high honors were concerned, was to be feared. The last cargo from here for Japan in April with the ships Rammekens, Ougly, Gulde Leeuw, in company with the hooker De Baers and the Pimpelmees with Malacca's needs, departed, and there in Buijenskercke and Nieuw Noortwijck to the amount of 555,925 guilders [modern equivalent: Dutch currency], 17 shillings, 6 pence, having been transshipped, is from Malacca, after it through Batavia, as there embarked to a sum of 604,150 guilders [modern equivalent: Dutch currency], 16 shillings, 10 pence, was

text_translated_detailed: Batavia. To His Excellency the Honorable Mister Joan Plaetsuijker, Governor General, and the Esteemed and Honorable Gentlemen Councillors of the Netherlands India. Esteemed, Most Honorable and Most Generous Gentlemen and Commanding Gentlemen. The fluyt the Black Lion on the 27th of June, the galiot the Brack on the 12th from Gale over Masulipatnam, and the small boat the Baers on the 22nd of July—here from Malacca, God be praised, have appeared. Through your Excellency's letters in copy of the 22nd of April and the original of the 28th of May, which we received from Colombo from the Honorable Mister Rijcklof van Goens of the 14th, and from Gale the 6th and 18th, that from Masulipatnam of the last [month], as well as from Malacca of the 21st of June, all of this year, we have been informed of the safe passage of the ships and cargoes sent from here for Japan to Malacca, Batavia, and Ceylon in the past season. We pray that the Lord will bring the rich capital of 555925 guilders, 17 stuivers, 6 pennies, which was transferred in the hulls outside the church and New North-wick from the ships Rammekens and Golden Lion, and further sent on the 6th of June last from Malacca's roadstead to Japan, there to a blessed market in good time. Having received from the Black Lion the sum of 81325 guilders, 6 stuivers. The Peguan silver per the Brack from Masulipatnam, 79159 guilders, 7 stuivers, 9 pennies. And the 99018 pounds of pepper from Malacca, 12713 guilders, 16 stuivers, 10 pennies. At the General Comptoir [trading post], together amounting to 173198 guilders, 10 stuivers, 3 pennies, properly credited here. The aforementioned letters from Ceylon, Coromandel, and Malacca go herewith in copy, although we trust that your Excellency will have received them before the departure of this [letter].

An uncommon violent whirlwind storm near the coast of Cochin and Tutecourin has caused the loss of the new costly ship Polanen and the Yacht Overveen (which had been laden with 581 lasts of rice, God forbid further damage), and because the chartered small ships with approximately 700 lasts of rice from Bimelipatanam through contrary winds to Ceylon have also not appeared, this double misfortune gives considerable shortage there. The Moorish equipment from these regions brought fairly considerable assistance of these provisions during the past monsoon, although in the beginning there was no great appearance for it. However, how great the quantity was, we cannot well know, because just those suppliers departing from here with pass certificates, sometimes finding favorable wind at sea, set course for the Maldive islands, and others again having their eye on it, through poor winds at the end of the monsoon, choose Ceylon. Likewise, the same has not been reported to us from Ceylon either. But because the Moors, through the recently obtained good price of rice and the shown care in the purchase of elephants, are now (with a reasonable estimate of rice here) encouraged toward the Ceylon voyage, the Bimelipatanam seven hundred lasts apparently stand to be sent there at the turning of the monsoon. Your Excellency shall also provide assistance from their ample supplies, and since one was oneself working diligently with the planting of that grain, I trust that such an influx in short will come about, so that from our side nothing will be necessary to contribute, otherwise,

An old moxudabatsen Governor Hazia Resa, through some accusation regarding the shortening of the Majesty's income, fearing the rightful authority of the royal dewan in Dacca, has fled to Patna, leaving his house, court, wives and children to the mercy of the Nabab, now awaiting judgment and decision of the majesty in Patna. In the meantime, another named Gozia Jnaijtulla has been appointed to that administration from Dacca, who, being greeted by the heads in Cassimbazaar, conducted himself in a friendly and willing manner, so that matters under the government are still standing reasonably well throughout this district. The under-merchant Harman Fent, second at Cassimibazaar, is, in consideration of the proof of competence he has given since November 1669 there, as well as by his provisional service of six months in the chief position at the comptoir Decca, and moreover in order that the importance of the comptoir Cassimibazaar and the other under-merchants might be governed with no less consideration, granted an act of provisional merchant upon your Excellency's— approval, as has been done in this situation many times, the same now requests by petition with all respect, as we also do for the allied reasons, to which we also reverently add that your Excellency would graciously be pleased to confirm him in that quality absolutely, and his salary, upon the ending of his contracted time (which expires in August 1671) according to your Excellency's good will to increase, in order thus to be— animated to serve well. We are so situated with the photas that the same will first be able to be sent with the ships expected from the north.

And therefore, by our letter of April 4th of this year, we submitted to your Honors the decision of whether the chief merchant Jan Velters or the assayer should compensate for the loss in refining the Coubangs into gold roupias to the sum of 494 guilders and 8 stuivers [modern equivalent: Dutch currency], on a quantity of 915 Coubangs, according to the previous mint standard that came up short. With the understanding that the first, who was held responsible for the assay, would have stood firm if he had used the customary procedure in the service of the esteemed Company with the appointment of commissioners. But since that was neglected, and now, as aforesaid, instead of 97, 99 gold roupias are to be drawn. Item, the diminishment in the refining—the gold in alloy improves, the same substance does not evaporate, the strong water indeed draws in the assay, but not for the refining or bringing the gold to higher alloy, with all effort and ability, and the adhering substance is entrusted to a person at 11 guilders per month, and who is thereby debauched, is alone trusted. So we thought we had some reasons, as declared on April 4th. But since your Honors are pleased to judge otherwise, we shall place the loss at the charge of this directorate and settle it, according to the present mint on the aforementioned 915 Coubangs, 1,114 guilders, 18 stuivers, and 8 pennies [modern equivalent: Dutch currency] coming up short,

text_translated_detailed: Ordinary Council and Governor of Ceylon. To the Honorable Lord Rijcklof van Goens, the Island of Ceylon with its Dependencies. Esteemed, Venerable, Wise, and Most Modest Lord. — My Lord, the fluyt ships Zoesendale, Spanbrouck, and the hookers De Bracq and Ijsvogel have been well delivered to us with your Honored letters, as those of 14 June, 21 July aforementioned, the Bracq over Masulipatnam, where previously for this trade there was shipped 3,679,159 rixdollars [modern equivalent: Dutch East India Company currency] and 7 shillings and 9 pence in Peguan silver, those of 30 August by the Zoetendale and the Ijsvogel, 24 and by the Spanbrouck, your Honored most recent writings of 11 September on the 7th, and also those of 2 September first on the 21st of this month by the small boat the Dolphijn with a cargo of 202,377 pounds, which reached Masulipatnam with 50 Oropien [uncertain: possibly a currency or measure] in specie and 31,072 pounds of Peguan rice. This small ship was from Masulipatnam to here in the river for 33 days on account of continuous headwinds and contrary currents underway, and we were already concerned about its journey and the feared Elephant, having also touched the Orissa Coast near the Black Pagoda to provide themselves with water, and where first 4, and later 3 sailors with the bookkeeper Brasser were left on land, without them being able to return by boat or daring to go back to the ship, so that these men upon coming to land face great hardships and poverty, since the Oriyas are a most wretched people. We are pleased that the ships and hookers sent from here in your Honored's past year have appeared safely, and their cargo was well delivered, and the Company's affairs, through the closing of the sound of the Island and good understanding with Raja Sinha on Ceylon as well as at Tuticorin and Malabar, stand in a reasonable state, except that our weapons, through God's blessing, have still achieved the desired successes,

text_translated_detailed: Copy 9. Daily record kept by the Director Constantin Ranst, Extraordinary Councillor of India, in his journey made by water from Ooglij [Ooglij: modern Hooghly] to Cassimabasaar [Cassimabasaar: modern Kasimbazar]. 29 August. The ships having been dispatched some days ago, and our presence in Cassimabasaar being needed to assess the new manner in the receipt of silk for ten days, we set out on the journey and at once gave the Merchant, Monsieur Pieter Hofmeester, passage to Canacoul [Canacoul: modern Kanakol] to see how the Company's guinastos [guinastos: uncertain, possibly a type of cloth or commodity], porrosaetdas [porrosaetdas: uncertain], and Madaboll [Madaboll: uncertain] are proceeding in the silk trade and the procurement of sugars for the service of the Esteemed Company, and through the visit to the Regents located thereabouts to show that the matters in the aforementioned Canacoul concerning the Esteemed Company are its own. On the first of September we arrived, thank God, in the evening without any delay at Cassimabasaar, having only received on the way letters from Surat, Agra, Patna, and Cassimabasaar. 2nd, the same. We had the Merchant Camkursen [Camkursen: uncertain, possibly a merchant's name] called and told him that his sugars from Birbhum [Birbhum: modern Birbhum district] numbering 5,000 packs must be delivered in Ooglij without any delay or excuse within 14 days, but as the same man appealed to the dryness of the River and that he would gladly wait until the Ganges grew somewhat, in order to bring that sweetness more easily by vessel and with less expense, yet considering that the Ganges had already fallen two cubits [modern equivalent: approximately 1 meter] and there was nearly no high water until now, and very little rain fell daily, such that according to all appearances the waiting for greater growth of the water would be fruitless, and this delay and dragging would only set us back from the concept of the planned early dispatch of the sugar to Patna to the particular prejudice of the Esteemed Company. Item, the aforementioned Ramkirsten, our long-standing [merchant], September, year 1630 [uncertain: possibly a date error], having made serious representations until now, as appearing to have been struck by the wind, since he has applied little care to it, I used somewhat earnest pressing reasons against him, saying that if at least no 2,500 packs at the aforementioned time in Ooglij were provided, then on each pack half a Rupiah [Rupiah: modern equivalent, a currency unit] would be paid less, in hope that thereby in our advantageous intention mentioned would not be set back.

Noble, Esteemed, Highly Honorable, Valiant, Wise, Prudent, and Most Generous Lords, High commanding gentlemen. 1671: To the Noble Lords, Directors of the General United Netherlands chartered East India Company, at the Assembly of the 17th in Amsterdam. Noble, Esteemed, Highly Honored, Valiant, Wise, Prudent, and Most Generous Lords, High Commanding Lords.

On the 9th of January of this year, I found myself compelled to send Your Excellencies a lengthy letter, which I hope, with the safe passage of the ships Beemster and Outshoorn, by God's blessing will have reached Your Excellencies well; and upon which I shall await Your Excellencies' final resolution in May or June next, concerning my departure or further stay. Such honor ought certainly to oblige me to gratitude, to obey Your Excellencies' commands, and to work with all my strength to deserve the trust that Your Excellencies are pleased to place in your humble and lowly servant, and to nurture and help make great the worthy child which Your Excellencies, as its fathers, have entrusted to me for so long according to my ability. I must confess to Your Excellencies that it is still tender, and consequently requires firmer nourishment for its sustenance, in order to gather its strength. My willingness to serve Your Excellencies under this Government for yet longer, I have shown in my aforementioned letter of the 9th of January last, and thereupon added in what manner I have requested to be supported by Your Excellencies through continuation, or otherwise to be honorably dismissed by Your Excellencies' grace. man who does his utmost ought to suffer. In this opinion I am also certainly not mistaken. text_translated_detailed: as any part on this Island, God willing that Pieter de Praauw recovered to health, whose illness (arising solely from heartbreak because his faithful service was regarded so little) has kept him with us, and who otherwise would not have remained for any consideration, if this man, I say, comes to health, he will be, and no one else whom I know on the land, the man to put Batecalo [Batticaloa] in order, and to extract from it for the Honored Company what lies therein; Cotiaar [Kottiyar] will later show what it is, and how much we have still not known, and in case Your Honors could resolve to place Nagapatnam under Ceylon, I would dare to judge, and standing against my opponents, that Ceylon would be helped, and from a weak youngster would soon become a stiff strong man, whose fear from the neighboring lands would soon be worshipped, it is also no time to delay any longer, or to slacken, but to put hand to the plow, and to seize the work without delay, before it becomes too late, for either one or the other (under Your Honors' wise correction) ought to happen, namely if our proposals are good to seize and maintain them, or else to turn the wheel over to another course, and to instruct us what shall be done or left undone, the work is now underway, Ceylon's harbors are all under our power and must be maintained or abandoned, for without possessing the lands completely, there is nothing to be gained, and our people at Batticaloa, Cotiaar, Calpentyn [Kalpiṭiya], Chilauw [Jaffna], and Trinquener [Trincomalee] will sooner die of hunger and perish from hardship than produce any fruit, indeed not even to keep other Europeans from the land, since our inhabitants then not obeying us must be hostile,

text_translated_detailed: reasons to love him very greatly, I nevertheless find still quite many remnants that oblige me to declare that I consider his long life and continuation necessary for the service of the Esteemed Company, since his respectability and wisdom still prevent much that perhaps concerning another would not be willing to follow, should it fall from the present council of the General Government into the hands of a person of more passionateness and less wisdom, just as it would weigh heavily upon me and upon each person to have to obey such a one. And to declare for Your Excellencies (as my benefactors) unfeignedly—I would indeed aspire to this (if it pleased God)—I declare that all my highest pleasure consists in the thought that (if God should still be so kind to me) I might once with honor lay down the service and come to Batavia to thank Your Excellencies, and thereafter spend my remaining days in quiet, honestly, so long as God shall grant me life, in no way striving after a higher position, since I have learned and found that it is all in the end more foolishness and vanity than wisdom. Your Excellencies please forgive me if I might have neglected myself here, or with too long a discourse, or something that might appear unpalatable to Your Excellencies, just as I expect nothing other from Your Excellencies' widely renowned wisdom and discretion. For since Your Excellencies yourselves are pleased to attend to this government, I would deem a successor necessary sooner rather than later. For although God has strengthened and spared me in fresh and hearty health for so long, almost miraculously, as I still thank God I find myself, such a thing could well change suddenly—Malaria [uncertain: "Malavia" may refer to disease or misfortune]—as we see daily in so many and countless examples. And with this matter concluding, I commend everything to Your Excellencies. Beseeching God that He take Your Excellencies together and separately with the state of the laudable Company into His Holy protection, remaining according to my entirely submissive and humble obedience, Your Excellencies' most humbly obedient servant from Colombo, 18th December 1670. Ryckoff van Goens

text_translated_detailed: Batavia to the Esteemed Lord Joan Maetsuycker, Governor-General, and the Esteemed Lords Councillors of India. Your Excellencies' most earnest, highly esteemed, wise, provident, very generous Lord and Esteemed Lords. With the ship the Hoff van Breda [Court of Breda], dated the 23rd of July, departed from Galle, we have received Your Excellencies' last dispatch as the copy shows, and since then we have received the fluyt ships Spanbroeck and Zoetendaal ready, with which the Lord van Goens undertook the resolved visit and journey to the eastern harbors of this island on the 2nd of last month, bringing with him approximately 100 soldiers and 150 cascarins [uncertain: likely a type of soldier or laborer], with which on the third day after our departure we landed at Batticaloa and arrived safely. The fort on the small island Pulian we found from the ruins in fairly good condition, but nevertheless made passable only with great difficulty, and so small in size that not a single warehouse could be built within it, yet nevertheless about 2 to 3,000 loads of goods will be necessary there. So that we, having considered everything with the Commander Vosch (who had come with us from Jaffnapatnam to Batticaloa at the same time), formed another concept of a more spacious fortification, and marked it out with 3 whole and 2 half bastions, and set the beacons, to which nevertheless work shall not be begun before first the entire land and all approaches are fortified, and when we shall also be more capable, not only to judge of everything and take proper counsel, but also to serve Your Excellencies as well as the gentlemen our principals with our sentiment to make a beginning here. Furthermore, the lesser chiefs and majors somewhat less in proportion to their service, in return for which they at once presented the Honourable Company with two tame female elephants, promising moreover to add one tusked and two other elephants, which had also been captured before our departure. This people is sufficiently powerful, being able to muster, according to the report of the Grauw [local leader], twenty archers, and consequently are able to defend themselves very easily against Kandy (with our assistance and governance established:). They are greatly mixed with Moors who possess such fine villages on the sea strands that they put to shame Billigam, Dondern, and Matur (as my lord the Governor-General knows:). They are of a different and larger stature than any people on Ceylon, moreover fat and stronger of body, from which it appears that they dwell in a land that produces abundant corn, cattle, milk, and honey.

text_translated_detailed: 5 Ao V 75 CA RCMLAN. Concept memorandum for His Excellency Commander Josephus Vosch, and Councillor at Jaffanapatnam. — Since the reports from Colombo do not permit us to remain here any longer, although it would be desirable for the service of the Honourable Company that I could still spend some time with Your Excellency to put necessary order to various matters, particularly concerning the redress of the wannias [local rulers], the provision of churches, and schools, and such other things as would be deemed necessary, yet since this is presently impossible, I have nevertheless thought it good to note the following in this memorandum, so that in due time and occasion some points might be further meditated upon, deliberated, and concluded with Your Excellency. — Regarding the wannias, I am of the express opinion that the disturbances that have arisen there for some time should be diverted to the utmost of our ability, keeping everything calm and in balance until a better opportunity, the enmity between the Caijla wannia and Ignatio Ferras shall also be diverted, particularly Ignatio Ferras shall be specially instructed to give the great wannia no cause for offense, and so that everything might proceed in better order, and the management of the wannias requires a particular man, we have already resolved in council by provisional arrangement to place as dessave [administrator] of the wannias the Lieutenant Harman Egbertsz, whom if found competent in this service we shall then have confirmed, and moreover add to him the rank of Captain Lieutenant, or whether the same might still need another lieutenant above the adigaer [officer] Ignatio Ferras, we shall be able to resolve upon further experience. — To better manage the wannia lands, I am of the opinion that the dessave ought to hold his residence at Ponnerij, or otherwise somewhat nearer to the pass, and that he should constantly have with him 25:

Three letters have come to us in the past season from Your Excellency, namely: of the 6th and 18th of June and 20th of August per the Moorish ship of the Governor Melck Cassum, and the galiot De Brack, as well as that per the Dolphijn, first on the 21st of this month, the said governors and other—nachodas, over the receipt of courtesies to Ceylon being well contented, that their prospect shall greatly encourage them to undertake the voyage thither again, which might turn out better than we now imagine, through the dearness of rice, in that no equipment through these years poor treatment in the Maldives, thither, (so rumor has it) is to take place. text_translated_detailed: From Colombo to Batavia. To the Honorable Lord Joan Maatsuijker, Governor General, and the Esteemed Gentlemen of the Council of the Netherlands Indies. Honorable, Highly Esteemed, Most Wise, and Most Generous Gentlemen. My Lords, On the 28th of October our last letter was sent to your Lordship, which herewith goes in duplicate copy. Since then (God be praised) on the first of this month there appeared within the river the ship Durgerdam and the hooker [small sailing vessel] De Molenaar, such that the ships of the great shipment from August from Batavia have all arrived here safely. And since the Blue Fisher and the two hookers (which we still expect from Malacca at any hour) will abundantly supply matters at the coast, and the cinnamon bark has been ready to send by hand, as the ships Durgerdam or Spreeuw, which must proceed first to make their late arrival and do the necessary work, have not yet taken on their full cargo, we trust that your Lordship will not take it amiss that we deviate somewhat from your Lordship's order in this matter. And now we are sending your Lordship the aforementioned cinnamon bark and the White Lion with 618 bales of silk for Japan, the Deccan linens for the homeland, 2,396 packages of saltpeter, 43⅔ lasts [modern equivalent: approximately 86-90 tons] of wheat, 35,632 pounds of catechu, et cetera, valued at ƒ376,458:3:1 [modern equivalent: Dutch guilders], praying to God that He will graciously guide the same speedily to your Lordship. The White Lion could have given its departure three or four days earlier, had it not been that we lacked small vessels to bring things out, which we find most urgently necessary, as the small vessel that is used here must also sometimes be set on the shore to be burned, or else the worm eats through it in a short time. And for this reason, the Tulip, having not been able to get a turn, has nearly become unusable.

And for this reason, the Tulip, having not been able to get a turn, has nearly become unusable, and although there are no sculptures behind it, the shallops—there is not much concern about them as long as they are light and suitable to venture four or five miles to sea and quickly return to the river. For the hooker the Black Fish cannot serve us this year, since it will arrive too late by way of Malacca, and when the urgent dispatches will mostly be done. Thus we respectfully request that your Lordship graciously send us a prepared and refitted shallow-draft vessel with the first ships (to be sent from here in May). We had already shipped silver to be minted at Ragimahol, but since we have since been permitted to refine our silver and gold within the Company's lodge to bring it to the required alloy and have it minted in Colombo itself, much risk and expense have been avoided. And what in hazardous times gives no small peace of mind. In cash we shall see in Colombo what conditions and opportunities can be arranged there, always so that the Banians shall conduct their dealings under our eye, as they could not do before. The samples of the rope works have now also been delivered to us by the skipper of the Spreeuw, and of which now, of each sort of plumb lines, one sample has been sent back, having been tested from the first, which your Lordship will find. Yet there is still hemp to be had, but the homeland lines, as long as we work thus, so that each sort from the hemp cannot be used as it should be in the rope, it seems to us that the usefulness of this enterprise, of such fine appearance, is hindered, as we have said many times before. And because we have found that the spinners play the sluggard too much, and the spinning thereby becomes noticeably delayed, we have now agreed that each spinner (among whom the wheel-turner is also counted) shall daily deliver spun yarn, namely 4½ pounds of sail yarn, 7 pounds of first quality yarn, 8 pounds of second quality, and 13 pounds of tally yarn. So that the hackling and clopping workers, for the preparation of the hemp to make sail yarn, being excluded from this (and who nevertheless must also seek their task to be assigned, or whether the hemp is to be delivered so fine by contract that only a small number will be needed), the overseers of the enterprise need not regard anything except that nothing is neglected and the thread is spun evenly. And with which we think we shall profit something, but whether they can spin 4½ pounds of sail yarn daily is doubtful, and which in a short time we shall experience.

Collated and agrees, in Ougly on the 10th of November 1670. — Pieter Noortman

text_translated_detailed:
To the Esteemed Mr. Constantin Ranst, Extraordinary Councillor of India and Director in Bengal, Most Esteemed, Honorable, Wise, Prudent, and Most Generous Sir,

My humble letters to Your Esteemed Lordship were recently sent on the 25th of the month of July, along with a parcel enclosed in sealed Surat papers, of which we do not doubt that Your Esteemed Lordship will have received them at the proper time upon receipt of this letter, as they had already passed Pettena [Pettah], and were delivered by good express messengers. It was on the 17th of September that Your Esteemed Lordship's well-intentioned writing and the packet attached thereto for Surat, sent by a runner from the aforementioned Pettena, came into my hands; which also shortly thereafter proceeded in that direction with further address, so that one can only presume that the proper dispatch from here was obtained, as Your Esteemed Lordship is pleased to consider.

News from the Royal Court and how matters are proceeding between Prince Sultan Masem and his father cannot be rightly advised upon, since for some time now no news from the Deccan [Deccan region] has come other than what His Majesty keeps very secretly to himself, which has come here. However, we wish by this letter to inform Your Esteemed Lordship of what is presently being divulged here, and what each person may well believe to be true, we say most humbly that the last known uprising concerning Kashmir under the name of Zasousa remains as though it has come to nothing and is to be held as having no truth, because the King, who can no longer help himself, makes no effort to send anyone there. Teijdachan [Teijdachan] holds with his army near Qualeer [Qualeer] still to carry out his King's command, to support the incoming Prince from the Deccan or Zuwagie [Zuwagie], and to completely observe the affairs of Delilohan [Delilohan]; it is said that he stands against Prince Sultan

text_translated_detailed: In the year 1670, on the 7th of October, on a Tuesday morning, having come before His Excellency the Admiral, Dom Belchior Suaris, Canangraij Modeliaer of Belligame, Dom Philipo Nechingachenadraija Modelaer, Receiver of Belligamme, Dom Manuel Chenerattena Modliaer Receiver of Baddamratchie, Don Simao Ragia Najaga Modljaer of Carredieve, Dom Gaspaer Consie Commare Modljar of Naloer, Dom Gaspaer Wereiltoja Modljaer of Belligamme, Dom Anthonij Canagarata also Modljaer of Belligamme, and Philipo Fernando Kitemalana Receiver of the Province Timmeratchie, have declared that they find themselves compelled to lodge a complaint with His Excellency against the Brahmin Timmersa, or at the very least he who presents himself as a Brahmin, who is a foreigner, his father being of the Casta Congani, born and raised on the Malabar coast, and named Timmersa, from which the son takes his name, but his true name is otherwise, Genesia Naiaka. His father Timmersa was, in the time of the Portuguese, on account of his arrogance, pride, and other unbearable qualities, driven away from here. It appears now that his son is following in those footsteps, being likewise arrogant, proud, and haughty, indeed so presumptuous and disdainful that whenever anyone, whether Christian or other inhabitant, comes to him and does not place their hands together and raise them in the manner of salutation (sombaijen) as they are accustomed to do before their highest authority, he threatens such people with such evil treatment toward the Commander or the Dessave that they would be sufficiently ruined. They further declare that he knows how to keep people in such subjection that no one has the heart or courage to lodge complaints about his abuses, violence, or other matters before those to whom it is proper, and many dare not even undertake to oppose him. text_translated_detailed: There appeared before the undersigned appointed commissioners the widow Arranck Agoddege Radda Mandrime, born from the seven Corles, presently residing in the Billigal Corle in the village of Arandore, head over a troop of Lascaryns [Lascars], approximately 41 years of age. The same, at the requisition of the Most Excellent Lord Admiral and Governor Rijckloff van Goens, and upon the interpretation of Mattijs de Silve Apohamij from the Singalese into Portuguese language being made, deposes to be true that His Majesty General Ragia Cinga, approximately 18 years ago, having departed from Wintenese Bos to the city of Badoele, would have taken his way toward Oena and in the village of Weeselij. There His Majesty Aftana Commara, son of Wiedjepalle Astana, King of Matule, had him come to him. And from there His Majesty with the aforementioned Aftana Commara proceeded through the middle of the Mende Corle over Openaacke and Battugiddere to the village of Kendangamme, located in the Currewijte Corle, accompanied by all the chiefs and great men except the Dessaves of the 4th, 3rd, and 7th Corles, as well as the Dessave of Saffragam, who each remained in their respective Dessaveship. At Kendangamme His Majesty became displeased with the aforementioned Astana Commara, whereupon he had him taken away, allowing his way to proceed through the 3rd, 4th, and 7th Corles to the village of Lackgelle, located in Lackgellewannij or Oedegodde Asckerij, where this Astana Commara was lodged at the house of the Majoraal of that village and remained there. Meanwhile His Majesty proceeded from Kendangamme over Algeretotte, Carrounelle, Bladtcopittie, Appoewijtewatte, Gannetenne, and Balene to the city of Candij, and from there again to the lower lands, and subsequently to the city of Uijlobe, returning there. At that place His Majesty had certain people put to death on account of some treason: Sattenoere Attepar Modlia, Gombere Henradt Modliar, Peraduin Dessave of the four Corles, the Dessave of Eens Rampotte Raale Adigaar, Condembij Raale, Hittij Banaijcke Raale, Wannoeke Raale.

text_translated_detailed: Rijckloff van Goens, at the request of Mattijs de Silva Apohamij, made from the Singalese language into the Portuguese, declares how now approximately thirteen years ago, he removed himself from his house and from the village of d' Imboelgamme to the village of Lacgelle to the house of the Mayorael named Sourg Hamg, where at that time the Prince of Matule named Astana Commare (son of the King of Matule Wiedjapale Astane) was staying, and had remained there for two and a half years already. One day after the deponent had arrived at the house of the aforementioned Mayoraal of Lacgelle, there appeared by order of his majesty Raja Singa a Tissobe Moutiaer with more than fifty lasca [uncertain: possibly a unit of measurement or military unit], who surrounded the house of the said Mayoraal all around, which according to our calculation was in the evening around seven o'clock. When the deponent learned of this, he left the house and hid himself in a small wood close to the said house, from which wood the deponent soon observed that the aforementioned Moetiaer with his troops brought the aforementioned Prince Aftana Comara out of the house and led him away. The deponent remained in the aforementioned wood the entire night, and the next day (after the aforementioned Tissobe Moetiaer with his troops had returned from there back up) the deponent came forth, and after inquiring about the aforementioned Prince, he was informed that the same had been brought to the water gate of that village by order of his Majesty to be hanged—

text_translated_detailed: Astana Coning of Matule had him brought from there upward, the said Astana Commara accompanied with a mudeliar [official] of Jaffana, four servants, a washer, a cook, and a female elephant called Jasapattij, in passing in the house of the attestant's father came to lodge, had that prince at that time but a white cloth around his lower body and the upper body naked, which he attestant then asked of the said prince's servants, why the prince was so poorly clothed, was, who thereupon gave the attestant as answer, that the prince had fallen into disfavor with the king, and after the said prince with his company had tarried in the house of the attestant's father for fifteen days, they went from there to the village of Wattoere in the Andepandoene Corle, where the named prince lodged at the house of the major called Mendowoll Ganmiddere, from where the same was further brought upward, the deponent having heard about two and a half years thereafter for the truth, that His Majesty this Astana Commara in the village of Lacgelle had been brought to be hanged, declaring further that Astana Commara was very well made of body, round of face and not tall of stature, and on his right arm had a black mark brought into the world, and he deponent himself had seen such, where the person who presents himself as the prince of Matule, and was sent to Batavia, (whom he deponent declares to have seen several times in the Hegampele Corle) was long and broad of body as well as long of face, without having the aforementioned mark on his right arm, giving as reasons for knowledge both the named persons, as well the prince as the one who presents himself as such, with own eyes seen, and all the recounted with ears heard,

text_translated_detailed: From the Attulegam Corle and the village Mangiddere (where the aforementioned prince had lodged for some days at the house of an old inhabitant) he came to camp. In the village Wattoere, at the house of Mendewillegamme Giddere, it was then that on that same day his Majesty Raja Singa arrived in the village Opowijte Watte, located in Andepandoene Corle. On the following day, some of his Majesty's people came to the aforementioned prince (who wore only a white cloth around his lower body and had his upper body naked), saying that his Majesty had become increasingly displeased with the prince, and had ordered that he be taken away, whereupon the aforementioned prince was brought by a separate route to the village Lacgelle, where the aforementioned prince Astana Comara, after approximately two and a half years of residence (as the deponent at that time heard it for the truth, and it was recounted to him), would have been put to death by order of his Majesty around the neck. The deponent further declared that Astana Comara was a person of high stature, round in appearance, and the deponent, giving as reasons for his knowledge that he had seen and heard all the foregoing with his own eyes and ears; and therefore being ready to strengthen this his deposition when needed, with an oath in the Singhalese manner, thus done in the field camp of Arandure on the 4th of December 1669 in the presence of François Montanier, merchant, and Pieter de Grauwe, dessave [chief administrator], as commissioners specially charged with this task. It was signed with some characters, and beside it stood: this is the mark of Andepandoene Corle Wattoercken Canangamme Jamme. Beside us present as commissioners Montanier and Pieter de Grauwen. Some more characters, beside which stood as interpreter: this is the mark of Narrangode Apuhamij, called Dom Joan, Lower in my De Bos knowledge. A meo [by me]. The aforementioned Attulegam Corle Mangiddere Oedewonegij Raddele, about 55 years of age or thereabouts, appeared before the aforementioned commissioners, which at the requisition of the Esteemed Lord Admiral and Governor of this Island Rijkhoff van ne Goens, through the interpretation of Mattijs Dasilva Appuhamij, done from the Singhalese into the Portuguese language, declared that approximately 17 years ago, his Majesty Raja Singa from Battigidere through Candangamme and Panuel came to the village Carrananelle, and for some displeasure with Astane Comara, son of Wiedjapalleastana, in his lifetime king of Matule, had him brought from there upward. The aforementioned Astana Comara was accompanied by a modiaar [official] from Jaffanapatnam, a servant, a washer, a cook, and a female elephant called Sahapittij. In passing, he came to lodge in the attestant's house, having a prince who at that time wore only a white cloth around his lower body and had his upper body naked. The attestant therefore asked the servants of the prince why the prince was so poorly clothed, to which the attestant received the answer that the prince had fallen into the King's disfavor, and after the aforementioned prince with his company had tarried in the attestant's house for 15 days, they departed from there to the village Wattoera and to Andepandoene Corle, where the aforementioned prince lodged at the house of the majoraal [major official] called Mendoewe Gammegiddere, from where the same was further taken upward. The deponent heard for approximately two and a half years thereafter, for the truth, that his Majesty had this Astana Commara put to death by the neck in the village Lackgelle. The deponent further declared that the aforementioned Astana Commara was very well made of body, round in appearance, and the aforementioned prince, with his own face and not tall in stature was; giving as reason for knowledge the aforementioned prince with his own eyes

R: Db: Vos — Compareerde voor de bovengenomineerde gecommitteerde attecalan corle Iasonder coralege cafvaegij apuhame out ongevaer de 25 Jaren en Eengada galle noere nagahawiedie wattoe neijndegij sierewedde hamij out 31 Jaren dewelcke ter requisitie van den Ed:le heer Admiraal en gouverneur deses eijlants Rijckloff van goens, op 't vtelcken van matur Lourens madere uijt de singalese Inde portugese tale gedaan, verclaren dat sijn maij:t Raja sing nu ongevaar de elff maanden geleden, ongedient wiert dat den prins van matule op rouanelle gecregen. en na colombo geleijt soudewesen waar over sijn maij:t gants vertooont sijnde seijde k hebbe soo veel grooten laten dooden, maar noijt sijn 'er geen levendigh geworden van waar comt desen nu te leven, die ick jmmers om hals heblaten brengen, en liet daarom tissobe moetjar, en matule oelangamme hieregij arache vatten, om reden te geven van den prins van matule genaemt. Astana Comara, welcke 2 hooffden openbaarlijck verclaarden dat sij haar ongevaar de 13 Jaren geleeden ter ordre van sijn maij:t met 50 lascarijns na 't dorp Lackgelle begeven, alwaar
text_translated_detailed:
Being translated into the Portuguese language, he persisted with the same, without wishing to add or change anything from it, confirming the same in the Singhalese manner with his oath consisting of these words: "May the god of heaven and earth be witness that what I have testified is the pure truth; if not, may God put out my eyes from my head and burst my belly." Done on the 28th of November in the year 1669, in the presence of those aforementioned, signed with some characters, beside which stood: "This is the mark of Mendebedde Hiem Mennick Belagagij Sonderahamij Nege Menijck Hamij." text_translated_clean: Singa Raju, whose aforementioned declaration in the Portuguese language was presented and translated into the Sinhalese language by the Sabander Dom João da Costa and clearly set forth, declared themselves to persist in all of this without desiring any change, diminution, or amplification therein, confirming the aforementioned Gale Gamme Adigaer the same in his manner with a solemn Oath, saying that God be witness that all that which he has declared is the upright and truth, and that God must preserve him as he in this matter has testified to the truth in an upright manner, with one his hand toward Heaven. Likewise he confirmed the aforementioned declaration of le Gopale Modliar with an Oath in his manner, saying that since he has no Quran here upon which he, swearing, can place his hand, he nevertheless swears as if he had it, and that he accordingly calls upon God as witness that all that which he in the aforementioned declaration has testified is the upright and sincere truth, thus done and passed on the Island Ceylon, outside the city and Castle of Colombo in the Company's garden called Hulffsdorp on the aforementioned day was signed with some characters, and beside it stood these characters placed by Gale Gamme Adigaer aforementioned, and also with some characters beside it stood these characters placed by Gopale Modliar aforementioned. text_translated_detailed:
I hope that the yacht Buijcksloot and the hooker [a type of small sailing vessel] that Swimmer P[...] and 11[...] of these departed for pepper to Malabar will soon come to light. Pieter van Banchem of Leiden in the year 1652 departed with the Court of Zealand. After he was condemned on the 30th of June 1653 to ten years in chains without wages to labor, on the 24th of October following, he was ordered onto the yacht Muijden without wages, provided that he should thereafter request to be restored to his previous position and wages if he conducted himself properly there, as appears from the copy of the account from the Negombo soldiers' books attached hereto. However, whether after that he fell in battle against the English and Portuguese galleons, or whether he departed further to Batavia, we have not been able to ascertain. But regarding this, in our letter of the 23rd of July last to Your Excellencies in Batavia, we have written that we trust Your Excellencies will be served with further information from Batavia, should the same person still be found alive.

Extract from Your Excellency's missive of the 19th of April concerning the goods left behind by the under-merchant Jan van Dalen. We have sent this to the Esteemed Commander van Reede and Council in Malabar and recommended it to Your Excellency's attention. He then also wrote to Your Excellency on the 16th of February last in such manner as the extract attached here will show Your Excellency. Beyond which we are unable to provide Your Excellency with further clarification. No free persons [civilians not under contract] came over with the three aforementioned ships Velsen, Soetendael, and Spanbroeck except Pieter van Dielen, who came to die very suddenly in Tutucorijn. His family has been placed in Jaffanapatnam with Your Excellency's approval. With Your Excellency's consent, we shall endeavor to obtain some respectable free persons for the voyage of the return fleet for two years, both from Batavia and Ceylon under the command of the Esteemed Extraordinary Councillor...

text_translated_detailed: ...to provide Your Excellency with further clarification. No free persons came over with the three aforementioned ships Velsen, Soetendael, and Spanbroeck except Pieter van Dielen, who came to die very suddenly in Tutucorijn. His family has been placed in Jaffanapatnam with Your Excellency's approval. With Your Excellency's consent, we shall endeavor to obtain some respectable free persons for the voyage of the return fleet for two years, both from Batavia and Ceylon under the command of the Esteemed Extraordinary Councillor Jan Thijsen. It was very pleasant news to us that God willing, we might at his time receive similar reports from the return fleet of the previous year under the Esteemed Ordinary Councillor Mattheeus van den Broeck, and that the ships which this year are to depart both from Batavia and Ceylon may arrive speedily and safely in the beloved fatherland. We shall, following Your Excellency's high commands as much as possible, take care that no procuration of earned wages be made except those which we believe to be justified. How many of these have been processed this year is made known to Your Excellency with Soetendael by extract. The Rhine wine came over quite rough and strong, such that it did not yield such advances as it otherwise would have done. The glasses, of which a quantity still remains unsold, have yielded through the other [sales] fully one hundred Rixdollars advance. He has answered that the settlement and transfer of monies would already have been accomplished if the heirs had taken the trouble to write a little letter in answer to what the administrators had written to them on the 28th of December 1668. Along with which they should also have enclosed a copy of the deceased's testament and estate, which with Soetendael is still to follow in copy. ...might render account and the remainder of their administration. Considering that this estate consists of debts and credits, and there are also four particular heirs to it, namely Bartholt Meeusen Roos, Jan Neeltjen, and Arjaentiw Couwenburgs, the testator's brothers and sisters, for this reason the administrators would not willingly make remission or payment of monies before they obtain from all the heirs together or their authorized representative a receipt and discharge in proper form, to be freed from liability. As they would also have requested the heirs in the aforementioned missive. For the provisions sent over by Your Excellency for the Governor's cellar, kindly provided, for this we are especially grateful to His Excellency and we all who also benefit from it are most grateful. Having nothing else to bring in return than to serve Your Excellency faithfully with our whole heart. Herewith then concluding, we commend Your Excellencies jointly and each individually to God's safe keeping, remaining Your Excellencies' obedient and faithful servants.

text_translated_detailed: We, the undersigned Joan van der Putte, skipper, and Jan Pieters Veltmuijs, chief steersman, in the service of the united chartered East India Company, stationed on the fluyt ship — (may God preserve it) named Soetendaal, declare upon the inquiry of the Honorable Commander Adriaan Agothaas, that the aforementioned fluyt ship (presently anchored in this bay, fully laden and ready to sail, in order to sail to the fatherland) being tight, good, strong, and suitable, well manned, with anchors, ropes, sails and rigging well supplied, and also well provisioned with victuals, moreover with ammunition of war, properly provided, in order to undertake the voyage to the fatherland and, with God's grace, to complete it, For which reason we hereby also declare that we can allege no reasons nor know of any difficulties to make known — for which reason the voyage to the fatherland with the aforementioned fluyt could not be undertaken, presenting the same if needed and being requested to do so, we strengthen this our declaration further. Herewith we enclose our reply to Japan, as we are accustomed to write there yearly, requesting that you be pleased to have the same letter forwarded. It is a fine capital in gold that has been brought to us with several of the 4 ships, mostly in Japanese copper coins and furthermore some other kind, amounting by the Malacca invoice, the aforesaid missing chest included therein, to well 14¼ tons of gold, and by the Batavia invoice still roughly 5/8 ton in the same metal. text_translated_detailed: No. 13: how the steersman David Loot is charged on account in favor of Ceylon, according to your order, over received money and missing pepper for Malabar, amounting to: further Comptroller General of India ƒ 951:7:—, just as this has also been transferred with the last dispatch to Colombo. Standing then also the former Company's Tolck [uncertain: possibly a title or position] there to be made known what you have been pleased to write concerning the jewels and gold pieces, for his account still remaining at Batavia. The things which your Excellency now newly demand from Coromandel, such as there are 10,000 pieces of thick gunny sacks, 600 pounds of hemp yarn according to the Bengal sample, 2,000 pounds of sorted carcai [uncertain: type of fabric], 1 last [modern equivalent: approximately 2,000 kg] of glass earth, 8 lasts of the finest sand for washing, cotton for the west coast as much as can be sent for the previous prices with sufficient ship space, and 15,000 pieces of coir matting properly made, yearly with their bandoliers and corporals, we shall subsequently also let come to your Excellency, together with all the others from the previous general's orders. Also, according to your order, until further notice, no more rags shall be collected for the Batavian paper mill, nor shall any more red and ebony wood be shipped than the ships need for ballast or caulking. Also, henceforth the cloth for Paliacatta and here around the south shall be given off for somewhat less than the previous prices, namely with for each guilder that it costs per ell [modern equivalent: approximately 69 cm] in purchase ½ pagoda to demand, in order to see whether the sale might thereby be increased somewhat, and with the benzoin from Baros one shall lighten the hand, even if only 15 or 20 percent profit were made on it, as it may not be more, because there still lies such a great heap at Batavia by the warehouses. The 1,000 pounds of cloves in fulfillment of Amersfoort's invoice have now been brought with Pegu unpriced and booked, just as your Excellency has also been pleased to write to us that this should be done. But as for the price of those most noble spices, since your Excellency has already ordered to reduce them to 85 stuivers [modern equivalent: Dutch currency] per pound in Indian reduction to other places such as Bengal, Surat, Persia, Wingurla, and Malabar, in order to increase consumption thereby, it is easy to think that they will not be able to be held in Golconda at the present value of about 14 percent higher, without the deduction there being seen to diminish considerably. Through experience, however, time will have to teach most closely. We have read that your Excellency allows, upon the proposal made by the Masulipatnam chiefs, in the Company's mine outside Masulipatnam, a thousand pagodas to be able to rebuild, for suitable or secure storage of the most valuable bales of cloth in the dry season, because in the city of Masulipatnam and around the lodge fire often used to break out. To the Esteemed and Excellent Lords, the Council of the Netherlands India, Mighty, Well-Wise, Prudent, and Very Modest Gentlemen, Commanding Lords, the ships Prince Willem Hendrik the 3rd and Dordrecht, together with the fluyt [a type of merchant ship] Binschoten and the Hooker [a type of vessel].

The aforementioned have arrived safely, with the first two having sailed from Nagapatnam on the 26th of May and the last two on the 4th and 7th of this month of June. As these were bound for Jaffanapatnam [Jaffna], we received these four vessels at the proper time, and with them your Excellency's gracious and welcome letters of the 22nd of April last. From the enclosed documents, we were pleased to understand that the ships from last autumn and those from this past year from this coast of Coromandel [Coromandel Coast] arrived safely at Batavia with your Excellency, and particularly also that the return fleet from the previous year under the flag of the Esteemed and Excellent Lord Jan Thijssen, consisting of 13 keels [ships], as well as the 4 ships from Ceylon and the two last sent from Batavia, all arrived safely in the fatherland. We hope that the Almighty will have brought the rich fleet of 7 sails carrying 45½ tons of goods with the Esteemed and Excellent Lord Mattheus van den Broek, and the 2 Ceylonese ships that were also sent out this year, safely home. His name be praised, and we give thanks for all blessings and pray with the fluyt Pegu, which your Excellency brought from Masulipatu [Masulipatnam], Kangasoen [a type of cloth], valued at ƒ197,885:1:6 [guilders, shillings, pence]. Your Excellency is informed that from there on the 19th of February, a value of ƒ62,511:7:13 was also sent to Ceylon with the yacht Buijksloot, which also contained ƒ10,176:12:4 in Palliacatta goods for

text_translated_detailed: Once again, you have been pleased to allow, with his wife Dona Ursela Falcoa, sister of the preacher D. Jan Terera, to come to Batavia. He has informed us from Madraspatnam that he thanks Your Excellency most heartily for such favors, but that his affairs do not permit such a departure at all! When it shall be convenient for him later to travel from this coast with his family on this renewed permission, we shall not fail to fulfill Your Excellency's order regarding those people, to arrange suitable accommodation on one of the Company's ships. We have granted Lieutenant Johan Askamp permission, at his earnest request, to depart for Batavia with this ship, since he is beyond the term of his service and is very eager to return to the fatherland. Having given us good satisfaction here in his service and comportment, we shall now have this garrison commanded for the first time by the provisional ensign Reinier Jacobsz, and we shall furthermore be able to manage well with the military officers present at Nagapatnam and Paliacatta, without requesting anyone from elsewhere for now. text_translated_detailed: The 2nd [of] 172 3¼ [uncertain: possibly a measurement or reference number] ARCHIVE Cape of Good Hope [Cape de Goede Hoop] To the Honorable Commander: Pieter Hackius and the Council. Earnest, valiant, wise, aforementioned: very discreet. Under date of the 30th of November last past, we have, Your Excellency, with the ship at home in Velsen [Velsen] thus informed, as the copy herewith attached dictates. Since then the ships Soetendael [Soetendael] and Cattenburgh [Cattenburgh] have also become ready, for whose escort we have directed ourselves to you, Your Excellency, by this letter, our aforementioned youngest request, to provide us generously with garden seeds, which we have now again thought good to do, and to specify to Your Excellency which seeds we would like here, namely: flowering savoy, cabbage and other yellow white carrots, sugar beets, red and white beets, white peas with and without shells, each part gray peas, radishes and rammelasses. The quantity cannot be too great. Lettuce, Latouw [uncertain: possibly a plant variety], chervil very necessary, cucumbers of the fatherland sort, audivi [uncertain: possibly a plant name], celery, Spanish melons, Roman turnips, and beans, other artichokes, asparagus, horse beans, buckwheat, barley, young olive saplings. The ones sent here are very likewise laurel saplings, well carnation flowers of all manner of colors and other flowers, grapevines of the best sort, rosemary, if it is possible, cuttings from trees that have not passed through the fatherland's hot water. Please do not send us parsley seed, Your Excellency, because it grows here as luxuriantly as grass in the field, just as likewise porcelain and many other herbs not mentioned here. We therefore expect good care from Your Excellency, which in some way shall be possible to fulfill, particularly we request that Your Excellency order for us from the saplings and peas each one vat full. These same and all other seeds shall here be received with willing thanks by the lovers with a certain profit, even if two were fulfilled, if it could be purchased for money. Also, it is highly necessary here that we ourselves be able to plant everything.

From the noble gentlemen commissioned managing directors from the respective chambers of the generals, united, Dutch chartered, East India Company, at the High Assembly of the Seventeen Noble, Highly Esteemed: Steadfast, Valiant, Wise, Prudent, Generous, most Honorable Gentlemen.— Commanding Gentlemen of your Noble and Highly Esteemed Assembly: Your most recent letters departed on the 2nd of November of the past year 1669, Joan Maatsucker, and the Gentlemen Councillors of India, wherein furthermore everything and that which we shall here adduce is also stated more extensively. We therefore find ourselves thereupon, in your good pleasure, proceeding further— By the letters of August of the past year, we have read with joy that the Return fleets from India in May and June of the year before had arrived home safely. God be thanked for his grace and that it has also pleased him to grant the ships toward this coast good voyages in that same year. text_translated_detailed: By order of the Honorable Rijckloff van Goens, Councilor of India, Governor Admiral, and Commander-in-Chief of the Island of Ceylon [Sri Lanka], the coasts of Malabar, and Madure [Madurai] with their dependencies, through the Honorable Adriaan Roothaes, Commander of the city and lands of Gale [Galle], Madure, etc., loaded in Gale's behalf onto the fluyt ship (may God preserve it) named Soetendaal [Sweetwater]. Departing from there under the bill of lading of the skipper Jan vander Gutte and Louis Warnartsz, Bookkeeper, consigned to the Honorable Gentlemen Bewinthebberen [Directors/Shareholders] of the united chartered East India Company residing in the city of Amsterdam, or their Honors' authorized representatives there. The costs and expenses of the same are as follows, namely: In Soetendaal for the cargo. In the Castle Colombo on the 25th of December in the year 1670. — 20,761 and 3/9 pounds of raw Persian, Bengali, and Colombo silk, consisting of 130 packs and one case, of various weights, types, prices, and numbered as follows, namely: Persian raw silk, packed in 12 packs, all together 9,440 pounds, wrapped in cloth and bound with rope, found as noted. Since Your Honors in the previous November under greater quantity, the Yacht Amerongen brought to Gale, and there in this vessel loaded, being of the following weight, color, and number, as: 267 and 9,410 pounds, making 23 and 9/408 cargas [cargo units], of 408 pounds Dutch, at 48 thoman or 4,800 mamoedis (of 8½ stuivers each) per carga. For which I set — Rixdollars 110,706 and 30 pounds. Upon weighing by opening, received pro rata for the entire lot, the remainder found untaxed — — — —. 9,440 pounds of Persian silk divided into 52 packs, cost of purchase Rixdollars 110,706, being sorted and numbered as follows.

text_original: Compareerde voor d'ondergenomineerde gecommitteerde weeuwoede arranck agod dege Radda mandrume geboortigh uijt de seven corles, present woonachtigh inde billigal Corle in het dorp Arandore, hooft over een troup lascorijns, out ongevaer de 41 jaren, den welcken ter requisitie vanden EE: heer admirael en Gouverneur Rijckloff van Goens en op het vertolcken van mattijs de silve appohamij, uijt de singalese in portugese tale gedaen deposeert waer te wesen, dat sijn maj= gen=t raja singa ongevaer de 18: jaren geleden uijt wintenese bos na de stad badoele getrocken sijnde, sijn wegh nae oeva en in't dorp weehelij genomen soude hebben, alwaer sijn maj=t altana Commara soon van wiedjepalle aptana Coning van matule bij hem dede comen, en van waer sijn maj=t niet ges: aptana Commara door 't midden vande nende corle over openaacke en battugiddere na 't dorp kendangamme gelegen inde surrewijte Corle trock vergeselschapt met alle de hoffsgrooten except de dessaves der 4:3: en 7 Corles; als mede den dessave van saffragam, die ijder in haer dessaveschap verbleven waren, op ken dangamme wiert sijn maj=t op geseijden aftana Commara misnoegt, waerom hij den selven: liet wegh brengen laetende sijnen wegh door de 3: 4: en 7. corles tot in het dorp lackgelle, gelegen in lackgellewannij off oedegodde asckerij neemen, alwaer desen aptana Commara ten huijse van den majorael dien dorps gelogieert wiert, ende sijn verblijff hiel onderwijle trock sijn maj=t van kendangamme over algeretotte carronuelle, bladtcopittie, appoewij te watte, gannetenne, ende balene na de stadt candij, ende van daer weder nae de beneden landen, ende vervolgens naer de stad uijlobe keerende alwaer sijn maj=t over eenigh verraet liet ombrengen, jattenoere attepatte modlia, gombere henrat modliar, peradumij dessave der vier Corles, den dessave van oena rampotte raale adigaer, condembij raale, hultij — banaijcke raale, wannocke raale, alloewandimij raale, sammere diewaeckere banaijcke, pasgamme
text_translated_detailed: There appeared before the undersigned committee a widow named Arranck Agod Dege Radda Mandrume, born from the Seven Corles [administrative divisions], presently residing in the Billigal Corle in the village of Arandore, head over a troop of lascorins [soldiers/mercenaries], approximately 41 years of age, who at the request of the Honorable Lord Admiral and Governor Rijckloff van Goens and upon the interpretation of Mattijs de Silva Appohamij, made from the Singhalese into the Portuguese language, deposes that it is true that His Majesty Raja Singa approximately eighteen years ago, having withdrawn from the Wintenese forest to the city of Badoele, took his way to Oeva and in the village of Weehelij, where His Majesty's Altana Commara, son of Wiedjepalle Aptana, King of Matule, had him come to him, and from there His Majesty, not [satisfied with] Aptana Commara, traveled through the middle of the Ninth Corle over Openaacke and Battugiddere to the village of Kendangamme, located in the Surrewijte Corle, accompanied by all the court nobles except the dessaves [administrators] of the 4th, 3rd, and 7th Corles, as well as the dessave of Saffragam, who each remained in their dessaveship. At Kendangamme His Majesty became displeased with the said Altana Commara, wherefore he had him taken away, allowing his way to proceed through the 3rd, 4th, and 7th Corles to the village of Lackgelle, located in Lackgellewannij or Oedegodde Asckerij, where this Aptana Commara was lodged at the house of the majorael of that village, and his stay there [continued]. Meanwhile His Majesty traveled from Kendangamme over Algeretotte, Carronuelle, Bladtcopittie, Appoewij te Watte, Gannetenne, and Balene to the city of Candij, and from there again to the lower lands, and subsequently to the city of Uijlobe, returning where His Majesty had certain persons put to death on account of some treason, Jattenoere Attepatte Modlia, Gombere Henrat Modliar, Peradumij dessave of the Four Corles, the dessave of Oena Rampotte Raale Adigaer, Condembij Raale, Hultij — Banaijcke Raale, Wannocke Raale, Alloewandimij Raale, Sammere Diewaeckere Banaijcke, Pasgamme

text_translated_detailed: Battouwatte in Billigal Corle Gandollepalle, approximately forty-eight years old, who at the requisition of the Honourable Mr. Admiral and Governor of this island Rijckloff van Goens, through the translation of Mathijs de Silva Apohamij from the Singhalese into the Portuguese language, declared that at the time when some ambassadors from Bengal arrived at the Kandyan court, which is now approximately [uncertain: number of] years ago, he, the deponent, was staying in the King's court. Which ambassador came to die three years thereafter, with whom there had arrived various Moorish servants, of which one, after the aforementioned ambassador's death, was taken into the service of His Majesty as a falconer, and from which service the same was discharged on account of some disturbances and placed in the stable, from where he entered into the service of a Brahmin named Baale Chrisnoe living in Kandy—whom he served for five years and learned some sorcery or black magic. From there he went through the landscape of Wannij (supporting himself by fortune-telling) to the child-goddess Corle in the village of Randumij, and stayed with a widow of a Jogij for approximately five months, whose goods he took and went to the region of Corle in the village of Wewoede, where he came to marry a daughter of a Sammerawellij Pattane, and abandoning his wife, he settled in Oudepalle Corle in the village of Pannelij, taking a daughter of a Doeneke Watte, with whom he thus lived long until she bore a child and he likewise left her, and went over Mohadije in the Halpitsigam and Billigale, and subsequently in the Gampele Corle, where he was caught by the Modliar of Ben and sent to Colombo, from where he (as the deponent has heard) was sent to Batavia [Batavia: modern Jakarta], since he passed himself off as the prince of Matule named Astana Commara, being long and broad of body.

text_translated_detailed: the modliar [chief administrator] of Jaffanapatnam with four servants, a washerman, a cook, and a female elephant from the attulegam [district] Corle and the village Mangiddere (where the aforementioned prince had lodged for some days at the house of an old resident) came to lodge in the village Wattoere, at the house of Mendewillegamme Giddere, at which same time his majesty Raja Singa, in the village Apowij situated in Andevan Deene Corle, had also arrived. The day after, some people came from his majesty to the aforementioned prince (who at that time wore only a white cloth around his lower body and had his upper body naked), saying that his majesty had become increasingly displeased with the prince and had ordered him to be taken away immediately. Upon this, the aforementioned Prince was brought by a separate route to the village Lackgelle, where the aforementioned prince Astana Commara, after approximately two and a half years of residence (as the deponent stated this time before the hearing as the honest truth and as it had been recounted to him), was to be put to death by order of his majesty. The deponent further declared that Astana Commara was a very well-formed person, round of face, and not tall in stature, giving as reasons for his knowledge that he had seen and heard all the foregoing with his own eyes and ears, and therefore was prepared to strengthen this his deposition, when required, with an oath in the Singhalese manner. Thus done in the field camp of Arandore on the 4th of December 1669, in the presence of Francois Montanier, merchant, and Pieter de Grauwe, dessave [chief administrator], as commissioners specially appointed for this purpose. It was signed and marked with some characters, and there stood: this is the mark of Audepandoene Corle Wattorekema Canangamme Gamme, bowing to the side. We present as commissioners Montanier and Pieter de Grauwe, also with some characters standing there.

At that time the prince wore only a white cloth around his lower body and had his upper body naked. The attestant asked the prince's servants why the Prince was so poorly clothed, to which the attestant's servants replied that the prince had fallen into disfavor with the King. After the aforementioned prince and his company had tarried in the attestant's house for 15 days, they departed from there to the village Wattoera in the Audepandoene Corle, where the aforementioned Prince lodged at the house of the majorael [chief] called Mendoew Gammegiddere, from where he was taken further upward. The deponent had heard for approximately two and a half years thereafter as the truth that his majesty had ordered this Astana Commara to be put to death in the village Lackges. The deponent further declared that the aforementioned Astana Commara was very well-formed

text_translated_detailed: to kill the Prince of Matule named Astana Commara, who was hiding in the village of Sackgelle, and to bring him to justice, which Moetjar, in fulfillment of His Majesty's order, proceeded to do with approximately 50 lascarins [soldiers], of which the deponent was one, to the village of Lackgelle, and there at the house of the Major of the village named Soerijhamij, the aforementioned Prince (who was lodging there) was brought under the order of General Moetjar and was seized and bound outside the house, and was led to the water pool of the village, which was not far from the aforementioned house, and having arrived there, the aforementioned Prince Astana Commara, by order of the aforementioned Moetjar, was struck twice with a bardisaen [curved sword] by a Matule oelangamme named Hieregij Arache, Cipher of His Majesty's prison house, the first blow entering under the ribs and the second from behind through the shoulder blade, after receiving which the aforementioned Prince fell to the ground, whereupon the aforementioned Hieregij Arache struck him with the same bardisaen a blow under the ear, and with this the Prince Astana Commara gave up the ghost. This all occurred in the evening at approximately 1½ hours Singhalese time, and according to our reckoning, approximately 7½ hours in the evening, with clear moonlight. After this death, the aforementioned Tissobe Moetjar had his lascarins keep good watch over the corpse the entire night, and when the aforementioned Moetjar in the morning had the Coij and Singhalese chair upon which the aforementioned Prince had slept and sat removed from the house of the aforementioned Major and thrown into the aforementioned water pool, after which, having eaten a little at the house of the aforementioned Major, the aforementioned Moetjar and his people departed upward again, leaving the dead body at the aforementioned water pool, giving as the reason for his knowledge that he had seen and heard all the aforementioned with his own eyes and ears, as being present throughout, therefore being well prepared to confirm this his declaration if needed and when requested to do so in the Singhalese manner, thus done and passed in the field camp Arandore on the 18th of December in the year 1669, in the presence of Pieter de Grauwe, Dessave, and Harman Dircksen, Lieutenant, as commissioned, and was signed with some characters, beside which stood this is the mark of Galla Baddegamme Carroena Pedia, on the side of us present as commissioned, Pieter de Grauwe and Harman Dircksen, also with some characters beside which stood as interpreter, and this is the mark of Colombo Narrangod, the apohamij [official] called Dom Joan, witnessed in my knowledge, R. de Vos.

text_translated_detailed: Moetjaer of the Moors, subjects of the King Ragia Singa Raju [Rajasinha], he Gale Gamme Adigaer being about forty years of age, and he Gopala Modliar being about sixty-seven years of age, now recently both sent by the aforementioned King together with Jasonder Appohamij, Gola Hella Appohamij, and Haccourouw Gammona Rale with the dead body of the former envoy Hendrick Draeck on the 21st of the past month of July to the court of the aforementioned King Ragia Singa Raju in Ditolleke, over which both Comparants [parties appearing before the court] with their men declared the truth in place of oaths at the request of the Dutch chartered East India Company to be truthful, that now about nineteen or twenty years ago (without wishing to be held to the precise time), when the King Ragia Singa Raju wished to come down with his forces by way of Ouva to Battigiddere, located in the Nandum Corle, then by order of His Majesty, at him Ragia Singa, on Wedilie (being a controller of Ouva near the Caddewette Corle), came the Prince Commara Singa Astana, son of Wiesse Palle Astane, who had been King of Matule and was the brother of the present King Ragia Singa Raju, and which Prince both Comparants declare that until that time lived in Kandy in the street called Oudenoere Wiedje, but that he (as said) having come from there upon His Majesty's order aforementioned, came with the King to Denuaka, located in the Agras, and by order of the King was placed at the house of the principal major-domo of Coetapittie, a village under Deniaka. That about two or three months thereafter the King (being at Battigiddere in the Nandum Corle) had the aforementioned Prince Commara Astana called again and ordered to live in Tippenauw, a village in the Correwitte Corle, at a place prepared for him by the King's command. That shortly thereafter, when

text_translated_detailed: Agras, and by order of the King it was arranged at the house of the principal major of Coetapittie, a village under Deniaka. About two or three months after that, the King (being at Battigiddere in the region called Corle) had the aforementioned Prince Commara Astana summoned again and ordered him to reside in Tippenauw, a village in the Correwitte Corle, at a place prepared for him by the King's command. A short time after that, when the King wished to depart from Battigiddere to Candangamme, located in the Currewitte Corle, His Majesty gave the order that the aforementioned prince should go to lodge at Carrawenelle in the Attulegam Corle at the house of a lascar [a soldier or servant of the VOC] named Oudoene. Also, the aforementioned Prince having been there for some days, and Ragia Singa of Candangamme wishing to depart from Carrawenelle aforesaid, His Majesty sent orders ahead that the prince should depart to Happowietewatte in the Handepandune Corle. A few days after that, the King came himself from Carrawenelle to Happowiete Watte, and having been there for a day or two, His Majesty had the prince travel with him to Gannitenne, a frontier of Candia; and there he had him delivered into the hands of Belan Toedawe Rale, who was then the Disava [chief administrator] of Matule. Also, the next day, the aforementioned Belan Toedawe Rale handed over the aforementioned prince to two araches [commanders] named Combale Olewe Arache and Matule Cattupoele Hoewadapoe Arache with their lascars, of whom the Comparant [witness] Galegamme was then the chief; and they declare that with the same they brought the aforementioned Prince by way of Matule to a place named Lack Gelle, located in the land of the Wannij, at the house of the principal major named Surij Hamij; and furthermore that the aforementioned major had the aforementioned Prince guarded in his house by the people of his village, as the Comparants declare.

The Comparants further declare both together that when the aforementioned Prince Commara Astana was brought from Gannutenne to Lackgelle, no more than two servants went with him, who were named Malia and Appoea, who are both still living in Lackgelle, and whom they, the Comparants, both saw depart with the Prince from Gannutenne to Lackgelle. Furthermore, the Comparant Gale Hamme Adigaer alone declares that after a considerable time, without being able to state the exact time, when the King Ragia Singa Rasu was in Nilobe, he ordered Tissobe (then Adigaer and Moetjaer of Matule), Carriapera Appohamij, Oeckoloewelle Mohandurem, and their lascars; also the Comparant Gale Gamme Matule Adigaer (being then still the chief of the lascars) with some lascars of Matule who are called Cattepoele, an Arache named Koeleheweij, and an arache of the lascars named Kattapoele to go to Lackgele; and that when they had come together there, on the order they had received from the King, they brought the Prince Commara Astana out of the house of the aforementioned principal major to a place nearby where the water for irrigating the fields is dammed up, called Rannamoere Ammoena, and that the Prince, standing near the edge of that dammed-up water, was pierced through by the aforementioned Koeleheweij Arache and Kattapoele Arache with their spears, so that he fell into the aforementioned water, and afterwards received several more stab wounds from many lascars.
